method: Thesis exposure = sum over open theses of posterior x value-pool weight (mandatory infrastructure 1.0, pricing power / scarce 0.9, abundant -0.3, new risk -0.6, loses pricing power -1.0). Final = exposure x (0.5 + opportunity/100) x (1 + gap/100) x technical readiness (trend template) x attention (not-priced +15%, crowded -20%). 'ready' = passes the book's entry gate today.

picks.why: The cleanest expectations mispricing in the set: gap +29 with reality 81 against pricing 52, meaning the fundamentals already delivered are far ahead of what the multiple embeds. It sits on the 'endpoint inference silicon and memory' layer of T-004 (posterior 98.3) and the robot/component supply layer of T-006 (88.7), both scored as gaining pricing power, yet thesis exposure is only 2.71 — the market treats it as a cyclical memory name rather than a scarcity-layer owner. Technicals are maximal (100, stage-2) with attention only 49 and not crowded, so the re-rating is not yet consensus.
picks.entry_condition: Buy on strength now while stage-2 holds; add on any pullback to the rising 50-day that does not break the stage-2 structure. Abort adds if pricing score closes the gap above ~70 without a matching move in reality.
picks.key_risk: T-004 explicitly requires silicon to loosen relative to electrons; if memory pricing is the thing that de-tightens in the next print, MU's reality score collapses fastest of any name here and the +29 gap closes downward rather than upward.

picks.why: Highest composite (7.42) and the only top-exposure name that is both technically ready and carrying a positive expectations gap (+15) — reality 83 versus pricing 69. It is the single stock that touches five theses, and crucially the three highest-posterior ones outside power: T-008 agentic finance interfaces and 24/7 compliance/surveillance (95.0, one flagged mandatory_infrastructure), T-005 adherence and titration agents (96.0), T-003 grid orchestration and dispatch software (92.4). The market pays for the AI narrative (76) but is not yet underwriting it as compliance and dispatch infrastructure across finance, health and power — attention is only 41 and it is not flagged crowded.
picks.entry_condition: Already 'ready' — enter on continuation within stage-2; scale the position in tranches rather than at once given narrative 76 versus pricing 69 leaves little cushion. Stop working the position if the stage-2 uptrend breaks or attention spikes into crowded.
picks.key_risk: Its two biggest contributions (T-008 at 1.80, T-002 at 1.55) rest on theses with different fragility: T-002 is the lowest-posterior major thesis at 81.4 and its falsifier — security spend compressing to 5-7% in a flat IT-budget year — would strip a third of the exposure. Valuation leaves no room for a single missed acceleration quarter.

picks.why: Largest thesis exposure in the entire set (7.75) and it is concentrated in the highest-posterior theses available: T-004 at 98.3 (power generation scarce, nuclear/SMR scarce, grid flexibility software mandatory) and T-003 at 92.4 (OEM pricing power, dispatch software scarce). Three separate 'scarce' designations plus one 'mandatory_infrastructure' is the densest scarcity stack here. The catch is honest: pricing 50 versus reality 58 gives only +8 of gap, technicals are basing/downtrend at 50, and it is correctly flagged watch not ready.
picks.entry_condition: Do not chase. Wait for the stage transition — a confirmed break out of the base with technical score moving above ~75 — or for a second/third hyperscaler disclosing a power- or permit-driven schedule slip (the stated T-004 next signal), whichever comes first.
picks.key_risk: Narrative 77 against reality 58 means the story is already ahead of the delivered numbers; if the base resolves downward, the electrification trade de-rates on order timing and execution even while the underlying thesis stays 98.3 true. Being right on the thesis and early on the tape is the actual loss mode.

picks.why: The purest expression of T-006 (88.7) — 'field labour aggregation (crew-owning specialty contractors)' gaining pricing power and 'skilled human capital itself' becoming scarce — cross-supported by T-004's transmission/mechanical EPC scarcity at 98.3 and T-007's skilled-trades leg at 94.5. It carries a positive expectations gap of +12 (reality 67 against pricing 55) with the lowest narrative score in the group at 61: the market is paying for a contractor, not for a rent-extracting labour aggregator.
picks.entry_condition: Technically 'emerging' at 62, so stage the entry: a starter now, the rest on confirmation of stage-2. Fundamental trigger is the named T-006 signal — Q3/Q4 specialty-contractor calls naming craft labour as the binding constraint with extending backlogs.
picks.key_risk: T-006's cleanest falsifier lands directly on this name: trade wage ratio flat and backlogs shortening. Comfort Systems is also the most cyclically exposed pick here — a data-centre capex pause hits backlog before it hits any of the software names.

picks.why: Security exposure without the security-sector overpayment. Where CRWD (-20), PANW (-18) and NET (-17) all carry deeply negative expectations gaps, FTNT is at +3 with opportunity 71 and reality 74 — the highest reality score among the security cohort. It sits on the same mandatory_infrastructure layers: T-004 trust/attestation for local inference (98.3), T-009 fraud and anomaly infrastructure (91.1), T-002 consolidated enterprise security platforms (81.4), and is flagged ready with a 100 technical score.
picks.entry_condition: Enter on the current stage-2 structure. Treat it as the security-basket vehicle instead of the higher-multiple peers unless one of those corrects its pricing score below ~65.
picks.key_risk: Lower thesis exposure (4.13) than its peers and no T-005 role, so if the security thesis plays out through platform consolidation, spend may concentrate in the very names that are currently overpriced. T-002's falsifier — security spend compressing to 5-7% — hits all five security names at once.

picks.why: Owns two gains_pricing_power layers on very high-posterior theses — endpoint inference silicon under T-004 (98.3) and on-device inference for continuous health telemetry under T-005 (96.0) — plus the scarce 'credential custody and the identity/preference graph' layer of T-001. Modest positive gap (+7, reality 66 vs pricing 60), ready, technical 100, attention only 35. It is the cheapest optionality in the book on the delegation thesis.
picks.entry_condition: Enter as a core, lower-volatility sleeve now. Increase size only on the stated T-001 signal — Apple shipping OS-level agents with stored payment authority enabled by default, or a card network publishing agent-transaction liability rules.
picks.key_risk: T-001 is the weakest thesis in the set at 57.2 posterior and contributes the most to Apple (1.60). If trusted delegation stays a 2029+ story, Apple is carried only by the silicon and health-telemetry legs, and a +7 gap does not generate much return on its own.

picks.why: Only name besides PLTR that is both 'ready' and carries a genuine multi-thesis stack, but it is the one candidate with an explicit negative headwind (-0.86) — T-004's community/ratepayer political risk (98.3, new_risk) and T-006's commoditisation of generic software labour (88.7, abundant). Positive layers are real: agentic interfaces to finance under T-008 (95.0, scarce), adherence and coaching agents under T-005 (96.0), grid dispatch software under T-003 (92.4). Gap is only +3 at pricing 56 — this is ballast, not alpha.
picks.entry_condition: Hold or enter as the risk-dampening anchor against the PLTR/MU concentration. Upgrade conviction only if the expectations gap widens above +10 on a print, or if the ratepayer-backlash headwind visibly fails to materialise in siting decisions.
picks.key_risk: The headwind is structurally identified, not speculative: at 98.3 posterior, community/ratepayer political risk on datacentre siting is nearly certain to bite, and T-006's 'generic software labour becomes abundant' cuts at the seat-based licensing model itself. A +3 gap offers no compensation if either lands early.

memo.portfolio_note: This book is deliberately barbelled across the two value pools the theses actually converge on: electrons-and-trades scarcity (GEV, FIX, with MU as the silicon-side hedge) and the delegation/compliance software layer (PLTR, FTNT, AAPL, MSFT). The concentration risk is honest and twofold — datacentre capex is the common upstream driver for GEV, FIX and MU, so a single hyperscaler capex pause hits three positions together; and T-002, at the lowest posterior of the major theses (81.4), underwrites part of four positions. I deliberately excluded CRWD, PANW and NET despite perfect technicals and dense mandatory_infrastructure roles: expectations gaps of -20, -18 and -17 against pricing scores of 88, 82 and 79 mean the thesis is already in the price, and FTNT delivers the same layer exposure at a +3 gap with the cohort's best reality score. ZS (+10 gap, pricing 47) and NOW are on the bench purely on technical readiness. The list changes if: MU's next print shows memory loosening (cut MU, it is the T-004 falsifier), GEV breaks out of its base (raise it to a top-two weight given 7.75 exposure), trade wage ratio prints flat with shortening backlogs (drop FIX), or any security name's pricing score corrects below ~65 (swap in CRWD or PANW, which have higher exposure than FTNT).
